questions.prompt: A crew sails once around Earth westward, counting each local solar day without a date-line adjustment. On returning, how should its calendar compare with one kept at the starting port?
questions.hint: Think about how following the Sun’s apparent daily motion changes the number of noon-to-noon cycles experienced.
questions.explanation: A westward circuit produces one fewer local solar day than staying at the starting longitude. The crew’s unadjusted calendar therefore ends one day behind.
